title: macOS Settings window and parented step-up sheet

setup: Start the S08 feature with the main window visible; confirm native Accessibility preflight succeeds without prompting.
actions: Record the initial main window identifier and geometry.
Send native Command+Comma from main.
Record the Settings window identifier, title, label mapping, logical geometry, and active-window identity.
Send Command+Comma again and verify the same Settings instance becomes key.

assertions.expected: Native Command+Comma input from main lazily creates one window labelled settings, titled Settings, at 1040x660 logical points.

assertions.requirement: Repeated native entry focuses the existing instance.
assertions.expected: A second Command+Comma leaves exactly one Settings window and focuses the same native window identifier.

setup: Start on main with no Settings window open.
actions: Send native Option+Command+Comma.
Inspect the main accessibility tree and on-screen controls.
Inspect native windows and active-window identity.

assertions.requirement: Option+Command+Comma preserves the main-window mock tool settings entry.
assertions.expected: The mock tool settings view opens in main and no separate Settings window is created or focused.

setup: Open Settings from main and record both native window identifiers.
actions: Select Security and capture pose S4-16 with Settings key.
Request step-up and inspect the native accessibility sheet relationship and active window.
With Settings key, capture main visibility, inactive state, and the whole desktop for any scrim.
While the sheet is visible, send a native click to the Settings Hide control and verify Settings remains visible.
While the sheet is visible, send a native click to the main action counter and read it back.
Record both native window identifiers and the main counter result.

assertions.expected: The Settings Security pose is visible at S4-16 and Settings is the active native window.
The step-up surface is exposed as one native accessibility sheet attached to Settings, not as an application-modal dialog or HTML overlay.

assertions.requirement: The sheet blocks input to its parent window only.
assertions.expected: A native click on the Settings control has no effect while the sheet is open; a native click on a visible main-window control succeeds and increments its counter.
With Settings key, main remains visible and independently usable, exposes the inactive-window state, and has no full-window scrim or overlay.

setup: Open Settings and record its native identifier and bounds.
actions: Select Team and use native wheel input to scroll its synthetic rows to a nonzero offset.
Send Command+W and verify Settings hides while main remains visible.
Reopen with native Command+Comma; verify the same window identifier, Team page, and saved scroll marker.
Move and resize Settings through native accessibility window attributes; record bounds.
Invoke the explicit test destroy control in main, then reopen Settings.
Record restored bounds and active native identifier; confirm visibility was not restored automatically.

assertions.expected: After selecting Team and scrolling synthetic content, Command+W hides Settings; reopening restores the same window instance, Team page, and nonzero saved scroll marker.

assertions.requirement: tauri-plugin-window-state 2.5.0 restores the settings label geometry.
assertions.expected: After moving and resizing Settings, the host saves state through tauri-plugin-window-state 2.5.0; destroying and recreating the settings label restores measured position and size. VISIBLE is excluded from the plugin flags.
The recreated Settings window displays the Team pose at S4-18, restores the same nonzero page/scroll marker, and exposes its active native window identifier.

setup: Open Settings and keep main available.
actions: Invoke the synthetic mock lock control in main.
Verify the Settings window is destroyed and a subsequent Command+Comma does not recreate it.
Invoke mock unlock in main and then Command+Comma.

assertions.requirement: A synthetic vault-lock signal destroys Settings; this is not a real-vault security claim.
assertions.expected: The explicit mock lock signal destroys Settings; shortcut entry while mock-locked does not recreate it; after mock unlock, Settings opens.

setup: Open Settings; retain the actual settings webview as the invoke source.
actions: Run the allowed mock command checks from Settings.
Open and cancel each parented host-run licence, import-data, and export-data picker; record native tree and parent window.
Run every deny sentinel and direct dialog plugin invocation from Settings; distinguish policy denial from unknown-command or transport errors.
Collect the CI ACL manifest, the S08 Rust authorization test result, and the resolved capability assignment list.

assertions.requirement: Settings capability exposes only its documented synthetic settings command set.
assertions.expected: Settings webview calls succeed for mock settings read/write, schema/search, shortcuts, step-up, host-run licence/data pickers, mock vault actions, project/team settings, view state, and hide.

assertions.requirement: Settings cannot invoke tool, pane, tab/project-open, MCP, marketplace, or direct file/dialog capabilities.
assertions.expected: Invokes from the actual Settings webview for every sentinel and the direct dialog command produce policy-denied results; no denial probe resolves successfully, and direct file access has no grant.

assertions.requirement: The Rust host allow-list independently rejects every sentinel and main-only command for the settings label.
assertions.expected: Rust authorization tests reject every denied sentinel and main-only command for Settings, and reject Settings-only commands from main; successful mock IPC alone is not considered proof of production capability enforcement.

assertions.requirement: Only the settings capability targets the settings label on macOS.
assertions.expected: The coordinator capability registry assigns no main, wildcard, or other capability to Settings, and the Settings capability grants no filesystem or direct dialog plugin command.

fallback: If any binding assertion fails or is UNVERIFIED, use the existing Windows/Linux modal on macOS while keeping Settings page content and step-up host contract; remove the distinct native-class dependency from the selected route.

verdictPolicy.pass: All binding assertions have resolved evidence from the declared native, recorder, capability, or CI sources.
verdictPolicy.fail: A binding assertion is disproved; select the stated fallback.
verdictPolicy.unverified: Runner, permission preflight, native tree, capture, or assertion pointer cannot resolve an assertion; select the stated fallback.
